court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Railway Claims Tribunal, Nagpur in O.A. No.(IIu)/No.RCT/ NGP/377/2012
case_name: Khusal S/O Nilkanthrao Barahate And ... vs Union Of India Through The General ...

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Khushal S/o Nilkanthrao Barahate, aged about 66 Yrs., Occ. Labour, and Smt. Chandrakala W/o Khushal Barahate, aged 61 Yrs., Occ. Household.
parties.respondent_defendant: Union of India, through The General Manager, Central Railway C.S.T. Mumbai.

facts_of_case: The deceased Prashant died in a railway accident on 20.4.2012 while returning to Nagpur from Warora by Express Train. The claimants are the parents of the deceased and have filed an appeal against the dismissal of their death claim.

legal_principles.principle: The condition of the body cannot be used to deny that an incident was an untoward incident.
legal_principles.held: In those cases also, the body was cut into two halves but this Court held that, the condition of the body cannot, in any way, be used to deny that the incident was an untoward incident.
cited_cases: Megha w/o Vijay Thakur and Another vs. Union of India (2020) Mh.L.J.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the respondent to prove that an incident was not an untoward incident.
legal_principles.held: The respondent has failed to discharge its burden under Section 123(c)(2) of Railways Act to prove that it was not an 'untoward incident'.
